summary.headline: The Trails Committee finalized plans for a roughly $450,000 CPC application for the Peninsula Trail bridge and approved emergency tool replacements.
summary.summary: The Trails Committee reviewed its upcoming Community Preservation Committee application for the Peninsula Trail bridge project, estimating a total request of around $440,000 to $450,000. Members discussed security improvements following a recent break-in and tool theft at their storage shed. The committee unanimously voted to authorize year-end budget expenditures to replace stolen power tools, purchase a gas-powered walk-behind trimmer mower, and acquire event supplies for Heritage Day. The committee also agreed to explore applying for a Choate Fund grant before the July 31 deadline.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee opened the meeting with a roll call and postponed approval of previous meeting minutes until the next meeting. At the conclusion of business, the committee voted to adjourn.
key_details: Meeting opened at 6:39 PM.
Minutes approval was tabled to the next meeting.
Adjourned at 7:40 PM.

topics.title: Boardwalk materials and conservation regulations
topics.summary: The committee consulted with a guest regarding the materials used by the Southborough Open Land Foundation for a prior Eagle Scout boardwalk near Bigelow Road. The chair noted ongoing research into whether modern copper-based pressure-treated lumber is permissible near wetlands before presenting trail project specifications to the Conservation Commission.
key_details: Discussion touched on past Scout boardwalk construction on the Callender Trail.
Scouts had reportedly been advised to use cedar or non-pressure-treated wood near wetlands.
The chair is compiling modern treated wood specifications to discuss with the Conservation Commission.
topics.outcome: Informational discussion with no formal action taken.

topics.title: Peninsula Trail Phase 2 CPC funding application
topics.summary: The committee prepared its upcoming Community Preservation Committee application for Phase 2 of the Peninsula Trail. Following a trail rerouting during a June work party, the project will focus entirely on the bridge and abutments rather than a boardwalk. Using a formula of 65 percent of the highest vendor bid plus contingency and cost-escalation buffers, the committee estimated the total bridge project cost at approximately $440,000 to $450,000, which will request extending an existing $211,000 CPA appropriation and seeking additional town funds while pursuing state grant offsets.
key_details: The boardwalk component was eliminated after rerouting the trail onto dry ground.
Estimated bridge and abutment cost is roughly $305,000, rising to $440,000 to $450,000 with contingencies and anticipated price inflation into 2027.
The committee plans to request extensions and additional CPA funds at Fall Town Meeting.
MassTrails grant applications will be submitted in February to help offset CPA funding if awarded.
Draft application will be circulated to members on July 1 ahead of the July 2 submission deadline.
topics.outcome: The chair will draft and submit the application by the July 2 deadline.
topics.why_it_matters: The project will determine whether Southborough secures CPA funds and state grants to install a major pedestrian bridge connecting town trail systems.

topics.title: Tool shed break-in and security measures
topics.summary: The chair reported that the committee's tool shed was broken into between May 31 and June 12, with approximately $500 worth of power tools stolen. The town will not file an insurance claim due to the low dollar amount. The committee debated security solutions including battery- or solar-powered trail cameras, motion-sensor alarms, window security bars, and a heavy-duty steel lockbox bolted to the floor.
key_details: Thieves broke the door handle, took the padlock, and stole cordless power tools.
Tool batteries were stored off-site and were not stolen.
A police report was filed with the Southborough Police Department.
Options under review include solar security cameras, motion-detecting sirens, and a steel job box bolted to the floor.
topics.outcome: Committee will pursue physical security upgrades and security camera options.

topics.title: Tool replacements and year-end equipment purchases
topics.summary: The committee reviewed plans to expend remaining FY24 budget funds before the June 30 fiscal year deadline. Purchases include replacing the stolen cordless tools, purchasing a walk-behind DR string trimmer mower for overgrown trail maintenance, acquiring event equipment for Heritage Day, and ordering promotional feather flag banners. The committee voted unanimously to authorize the chair to execute the expenditures, estimated between $2,000 and $3,000.
key_details: Replacement tools include a Worx cordless drill, mini chainsaw, pole saw, hedge trimmer, and backup batteries.
A gas-powered DR trimmer mower was approved for $459.99 plus maintenance accessories.
Heritage Day event supplies include two folding tables, folding chairs, fitted tablecloths, a canopy tent with sidewalls, and sandbags.
Committee authorized promotional teardrop flag banners featuring the committee logo and website.

topics.title: Choate Fund recreation grant opportunity
topics.summary: The chair announced that applications are open for the Choate Fund public recreation grant program, which offers awards up to $5,000 for capital recreation projects. The committee expressed interest in applying before the July 31 deadline and agreed to discuss specific project proposals at its next meeting.
key_details: Grant provides up to $5,000 for local public recreation capital projects.
Application deadline is July 31.
Potential uses discussed include trail signage and trail improvements.
topics.outcome: The committee will review project concepts and prepare an application at its July 16 meeting.

votes.motion: Authorize the chair to make expenditures for replacement tools, maintenance equipment, and event supplies as discussed.
